crime.value: Serial vigilante executions of violent criminals who escaped capital punishment due to state law abolition. Central question: Can the narrator prove Sam Zodiak's guilt, and does justice justify murder?
crime.quote: There've been five of them now, five of them since last year. The others were downstate, and didn't make such splashy headlines.

victim.value: Five murder victims (criminals themselves): George Condon (killed Ann, a nurse); an unnamed sex murderer named Asker; three others downstate. All had evaded capital punishment through legal abolition or mental health provisions.
victim.quote: All criminals, all murderers who'd escaped the death penalty because of our laws.

culprit_and_motive.value: Sam Zodiak, the narrator's former army friend. Motive: vigilante justice. After his fiancée Ann was killed by George Condon (a released mental patient), Zodiak adopted a personal code of executing murderers who escaped state-mandated punishment, framing it as moral warfare.
culprit_and_motive.quote: I'm a warrior in the battle for justice...You'd never prove it to the police anyway, so I'm safe in telling you.

resolution.value: The narrator, horrified and convinced of Zodiak's guilt and ongoing threat, murders him by pushing him off a bridge. No official investigation occurs; Zodiak's death is treated as accidental. Justice is achieved through vigilantism mirroring the crime itself.
resolution.quote: It was then that I pushed him with all my strength, saw him grasping frantically at the railing before he toppled over...

investigator.value: The unnamed narrator, the protagonist and Zodiak's oldest friend. He serves as both investigator and ultimate executor—moved by suspicion and moral horror to confront, then eliminate, the vigilante.
investigator.quote: I arranged to fly out there the following weekend...For a moment speechless from the horror of what he was telling me.
